editorial.purpose_and_first_use: Read the complete outline. Its plain title, goal and scenario introduce reviewing a concordato proposal and plan with Vera: provide files, confirm the assignment, review interpretations, open the actual report and workbook, and repeat with an update. The lesson covers the workflow from request to useful dossier. It does not make the amount-comparison appendix or an isolated financial exception the subject of the lesson.
editorial.inputs_and_request: The fictional Officina Riva case uses demo-it.xlsx and management-demo-it.pdf, with matching practice versions. The workbook provides the assignment, three declared supplier claims and annual plan. The two-page management schedule supplies invoice references, a management liquidation estimate and quarterly timing, with absent originals and uncommitted financing explicit. Both PDF phases were visually reviewed in this language. These files provide information to interpret; no approved analysis or case model is shipped as an answer. The natural-language request asks for creditor treatment, sources and uses, liquidity, missing documents and open questions.
editorial.execution_and_checkpoints: The current native runner captures both source files into a managed Studio Archive run and initially leaves the case awaiting semantic review. The regression supplies separately authored test-only interpretations, seals them through the native review helper with an explicitly synthetic reviewer, executes the real reporting pipeline and completes the archive declaration. It checks the three creditor positions and four quarterly cash balances. These tests do not claim live research, model inference or learner/professional approval. The outline places execution in the working chat and explanation/questions in the voice chat, with checkpoints for the requested work, supplied files, actual result and one source-backed next action.
editorial.deliverable_and_next_action: Reviewed the actual primary Word report in full and the actual Excel overview, creditor, treatment, quarterly liquidity and source-note views. Word and Excel retain localized labels, complete authored reasoning and source page/cell locators. The workbook source-note links are checked by the native regression. The primary reports show EUR 200,000 claims, EUR 130,000 proposed cash payments (65%), and EUR 90,000 management-estimated liquidation recovery (45%). They retain the missing accounts, contracts, attestation, tax/social-security scope, independent valuation and monthly cash forecast. The main report explicitly says the optional amount comparison was not executed. The learner opens the summary then Excel, follows one issue to a source and chooses a document request or clarification; the teacher is instructed not to read the whole report aloud. Internal review/archive files and the optional numerical appendix are not the primary teaching deliverables.
editorial.practice_and_repeat: The practice reruns the actual pipeline in a new run of the same engagement after importing both updated fictional files. Assumed finance falls from EUR 50,000 to EUR 30,000. Demo quarterly closing cash is 5,000 / 80,000 / 105,000 / 0; practice is 5,000 / 60,000 / 85,000 / -20,000. The updated report identifies the uncovered funding requirement and preserves the need to establish commitment, timing, repayment and monthly cash. Native tests assert every first-run file remains byte-identical. The learner is asked to explain changed results and next actions and receives a clear list of inputs to provide for a real repeat.
